notes: Overview: building an IDE copilot integrated into VS Code + web IDE. Primary product is a live assistant + batch embedding indexer for code search.

Requirements (summary): low-latency streaming for completions (aim <100ms end-to-end; prefer token stream <50ms), deterministic model pinning per release channel, and daily embedding refresh for monorepo snapshots (~5M files/trees).

Throughput: embedding refresh job expected to process ~5M file chunks/day. Prefer continuous batching + incremental KV cache. Want ability to run high-throughput background jobs without impacting interactive latency.
Routing needs: traffic split by environment (canary, prod), fallback to smaller models when Dedicated pool at capacity, region-aware routing (NA + EU customers).

Security: must support SSO (SAML), KMS integration for key management, audit logs for generation/access, 90-day retention for ephemeral logs, data residency requirement for some EU enterprise customers.
Cost sensitivity: moderate — will trade cost for guaranteed sub-100ms streaming for developer-facing features; background embedding pipeline should be optimized for unit cost.
Tech preferences: prefer ONNX/quantized models for background jobs, want per-route batching config via Redwood Optimize suggestions, need per-version pinning and safe rollback (canary -> full).
Quote from CTO on 2026-02-18 call: 'If we can't guarantee the editor experience, users churn. Low tail latency > cost reduction for interactive flows.'

POC ask: 48-hour Dedicated cluster that isolates interactive traffic from embedding workers (separate GPU pools), sample embedding pipeline demo with autoscaling and backpressure handling, and commit-level evaluate harness for regression checks.

Integration notes: VS Code extension will open persistent WebSocket streams to Redwood API; need token rotation advice and connection-level health signals. Also require guidance on prefix caching of common repo headers to reduce token usage.
Security review status: submitted security questionnaire (drive link), next: architecture deep-dive with Security on 2026-03-15. Need SOC2 cert copy and KMS integration checklist.
Procurement: procurement has initial SOW estimates; legal reviewing DPA. Budget committee meets 2026-03-20.
Internal AE notes: SE liked Redwood's automatic KV cache + fallback policy. Ask: get concrete latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for streaming on Dedicated 4x A100 baseline.
Potential upsell: if Dedicated POC meets latency targets, client will evaluate Redwood Private for EU-residency deployments and longer-term reserved capacity (annual).
